newsitem.title: USA: Harley-Davidson awaits next ruling in suit.
newsitem.headline: Harley-Davidson awaits next ruling in suit.

text.p: Harley-Davidson Inc, ordered by a New Jersey Superior Court jury last week to pay $9.9 million in compensatory damages in a product liability lawsuit, is expected to hear from a judge within weeks on whether it will also be ordered to pay punitive damages.
"She will probably decide relatively soon (on whether the jury will decide on punitive damages)," G. Martin Meyers, the plaintiff's attorney, told Reuters Monday.
A company spokesman said there will be no comment on the case until that decision is reached later this month.

The case stemmed from a 1991 accident involving Thomas Molinaro of Pen Argyl, Pennsylvania. Meyers said his client was seriously injured when a device that acted like a cruise control on his 1987-model Harley motorcycle did not disengage as Molinaro went around a curve on a road in New Jersey.

Molinaro was catapulted over the front of the motorcycle and thrown about 40 yards, suffering severe pelvic injuries, Meyers said. The attorney added that the accident crushed Molinaro's right leg, which was amputated.

Meyers said the next phase of the case involves Superior Court Judge Rosalie Cooper determining whether claims for punitive damages will be sent to the jury. Harley-Davidson is seeking to have those claims dismissed, Meyers said.
The Harley-Davidson spokesman declined to comment.
Meyers said the amount of punitive damages, if the judge decides to proceed with that phase, will be set by the jury, which also set the amount of compensatory damages.
He added the parties could take other steps, including filing an appeal, if the the judge decides not to send the question of punitive damages to the jury.
Harley-Davidson shares were trading up 3/4 at 43-3/4.
